pairs: Propter peccata quæ peccastis ante Deum, abducemini in Babyloniam captivi a Nabuchodonosor rege Babylonis.

This is a copy of the letter that Jeremiah sent to those who would be taken captive into Babylon by the king of Babylon, so as to prophesy to them according to the warning he had received about them from God. “Because of the sins which you have sinned before God, you will be carried away into the captivity of Babylon by Nebuchadnezzar, the king of Babylon.
Ingressi itaque in Babylonem,
And so, having been taken into Babylon,
eritis ibi annis plurimis, et temporibus longis,
you will be there many years and for a long time,
usque ad generationes septem:
even to seven generations, yet after this,
post hoc autem educam vos inde cum pace.
I will lead you away from there with peace.
Nunc autem videbitis in Babylonia deos aureos et argenteos,
But now, you will see in Babylon gods of gold and of silver,
et lapideos et ligneos,
and of stone and of wood,
in humeris portari,
carried upon shoulders,
ostentantes metum gentibus.
an awful display for the peoples.
Videte ergo ne
See to it,
et vos similes efficiamini factis alienis,
then,
et metuatis,
that you do not in effect become like these strangers and become afraid,
et metus vos capiat in ipsis.
so that in awe you would be carried away into their midst.
Visa itaque turba de retro et ab ante,
And so, seeing the turmoil, behind you and in front of you,
adorantes dicite in cordibus vestris:
as they are worshiping, say in your hearts,
Te oportet adorari,
‘You ought to be adored,
Domine.
O Lord.’
Angelus enim meus vobiscum est:
For my angel is with you.
ipse autem exquiram animas vestras.
And I myself will examine your souls.
Nam lingua ipsorum polita a fabro;
For their tongue is polished by the craftsman,
ipsa etiam inaurata et inargentata:
and they themselves are even inlaid with gold and silver,
falsa sunt, et non possunt loqui.
yet they are false and unable to speak.
Et sicut virgini amanti ornamenta,
And, just like a virgin who loves to decorate herself,
ita accepto auro fabricati sunt.
so do they take up gold and make designs with it.
Coronas certe aureas habent super capita sua dii illorum:
Their gods have crowns of certified gold upon their heads,
unde subtrahunt sacerdotes ab eis aurum et argentum,
from which the priests subtract gold and silver,
et erogant illud in semetipsos.
and spend it on themselves.
Dant autem
Moreover,
et ex ipso prostitutis,
they even give from it to prostitutes,
et meretrices ornant:
and use it to adorn kept women,
et iterum cum receperint illud a meretricibus,
and when they receive it back from the kept women,
ornant deos suos.
they use it to adorn their gods.
Hi autem non liberantur ab ærugine et tinea.
But these cannot be freed from rust and moths.
Opertis autem illis veste purpurea,
Although they are covered with a purple garment,
extergunt faciem ipsorum propter pulverem domus qui est plurimus inter eos.
they must wipe off their face, because of the dust of the house, which is very great around them.
Sceptrum autem habet ut homo,
Yet he who holds a scepter like a man,
sicut judex regionis,
like the judge of the region,
qui in se peccantem non interficit.
cannot put to death one who sins against him.
Habet etiam in manu gladium et securim,
And though he holds in his hand a sword and an axe,
se autem de bello et a latronibus non liberat.
yet he cannot free himself from war and robbers.
Unde vobis notum sit quia non sunt dii:
From this let it be known to you that they are not gods.
non ergo timueritis eos.
Therefore,
Sicut enim vas hominis confractum inutile efficitur,
do not fear them.
tales sunt
For just as the vessel a man uses becomes useless when broken,
et dii illorum.
so also are their gods.
Constitutis illis in domo,
When they are set up in a house,
oculi eorum pleni sunt pulvere a pedibus introëuntium.
their eyes are full of dust from the feet of those who enter.
Et sicut alicui qui regem offendit circumseptæ sunt januæ,
And like one who has offended the king and is surrounded at every door,
aut sicut ad sepulchrum adductum mortuum:
or like a corpse about to be carried to the grave,
ita tutantur sacerdotes ostia clausuris et seris,
so do the priests secure the doors with bars and locks,
ne a latronibus expolientur.
lest they be plundered by robbers.
Lucernas accendunt illis,
They light candles to them,
et quidem multas,
and in great number,
ex quibus nullam videre possunt:
and still they are unable to see,
sunt autem sicut trabes in domo.
for they are like logs in the house.
Corda vero eorum dicunt elingere serpentes qui de terra sunt,
It is truly said that the creeping things, which are of the earth, gnaw their hearts,
dum comedunt eos, et vestimentum ipsorum,
and yet when these devour them and their garments,
et non sentiunt.
they do not feel it.
Nigræ fiunt facies eorum a fumo qui in domo fit.
Their faces are made black by the smoke that is made in the house.
Supra corpus eorum et supra caput eorum volant noctuæ, et hirundines,
Over their bodies and over their heads fly owls and swallows and birds,
et aves etiam, similiter et cattæ.
and similarly, even cats.
Unde sciatis quia non sunt dii:
From this you should understand that they are not gods.
ne ergo timueritis eos.
Therefore, neither should you fear them.
Aurum etiam quod habent ad speciem est:
Furthermore, the gold which they have is shiny,
nisi aliquis exterserit æruginem,
but unless someone wipes off the rust,
non fulgebunt:
they will not shine.
neque enim dum conflarentur, sentiebant.
And even when they were molten, they did not feel it.
Ex omni pretio empta sunt,
They acquire all kinds of costly things,
in quibus spiritus non inest ipsis.
yet there is no breath in them.
Sine pedibus,
Without feet,
in humeris portantur,
they are carried upon shoulders,
ostentantes ignobilitatem suam hominibus:
showing their unworthiness to all men. And so,
confundantur etiam qui colunt ea.
may those who worship them be confounded.
Propterea si ceciderint in terram,
Because of this, if they fall to the ground,
a semetipsis non consurgunt:
they do not get up by themselves;
neque si quis eum statuerit rectum, per semetipsum stabit:
and if someone sets it upright, they will not stand firm on their own;
sed sicut mortuis munera eorum illis apponentur.
yet, just like the dead, offerings are placed next to them.
Hostias illorum vendunt sacerdotes ipsorum,
The priests themselves sell their sacrifices,
et abutuntur:
and they spend it wastefully;
similiter et mulieres eorum decerpentes,
and,
neque infirmo,
in like manner,
neque mendicanti,
their wives take part of it,
aliquid impertiunt.
never sharing anything with the sick or the beggars.
De sacrificiis eorum fœtæ
Fertile and menstruous women contaminate their sacrifices.
et menstruatæ contingunt.
And so,
Sciens itaque ex his quia non sunt dii,
knowing from this that they are not gods,
ne timeatis eos.
you should not fear them.
Unde enim vocantur dii?
For what reason are they called gods?
quia mulieres apponunt diis argenteis,
It is because the women serve before the gods of silver
et aureis,
and gold
et ligneis:
and wood,
et in domibus eorum sacerdotes sedent habentes tunicas scissas,
and the priests sit in their houses,
et capita
with torn garments,
et barbam rasam,
and their heads and beards shaven,
quorum capita nuda sunt.
and nothing on their heads.
Rugiunt autem clamantes contra deos suos sicut in cœna mortui.
But they roar, shouting out to their gods, just as at a feast for the dead.
Vestimenta eorum auferunt sacerdotes,
The priests take away the garments of their gods,
et vestiunt uxores suas et filios suos.
and clothe their wives and their sons.
Neque si quid mali patiuntur ab aliquo,
And whether they endure evil from someone,
neque si quid boni,
or good,
poterunt retribuere:
they are not able to repay it.
neque regem constituere possunt,
They can neither establish a king,
neque auferre.
nor remove him.
Similiter
Similarly,
neque dare divitias possunt,
they can neither give riches,
neque malum retribuere.
nor avenge evil.
Si quis illis votum voverit
If anyone makes a vow to them,
et non reddiderit,
and does not keep it,
neque hoc requirunt.
they cannot require it.
Hominem a morte non liberant,
They cannot free a man from death,
neque infirmum a potentiori eripiunt.
nor rescue the weak from the strong.
Hominem cæcum ad visum non restituunt;
They cannot restore sight to the blind,
de necessitate hominem non liberabunt.
nor free a man from need.
Viduæ non miserebuntur,
They will not have mercy on the widow,
neque orphanis benefacient.
nor do good to orphans.
Lapidibus de monte similes sunt dii illorum,
Their gods of wood, and of stone,
lignei,
and of gold,
et lapidei,
and of silver,
et aurei, et argentei:
are like stones from the mountain;
qui autem colunt ea, confundentur.
and those who worship them will be confounded.
Quomodo ergo æstimandum est aut dicendum illos esse deos?
In what way, then, is it to be supposed or said that they are gods?
Adhuc enim ipsis Chaldæis non honorantibus ea:
For even the Chaldeans themselves do not honor these,
qui cum audierint mutum non posse loqui,
who, when they hear about a mute, unable to speak,
offerunt illud ad Bel,
they offer him to Bel,
postulantes ab eo loqui:
asking from him that he may speak,
quasi possint sentire qui non habent motum!
as if these, who are unable to move, would be able to perceive.
Et ipsi, cum intellexerint,
And even they themselves, when they shall understand this,
relinquent ea:
will abandon them, for,
sensum enim non habent ipsi dii illorum.
having come to their senses, they do not consider them to be gods.
Mulieres autem circumdatæ funibus in viis sedent,
Yet the women, wrapped in cords, sit by the roads,
succendentes ossa olivarum:
burning olive-stones.
cum autem aliqua ex ipsis,
And when any one of them,
attracta ab aliquo transeunte,
having been attracted by someone passing by,
dormierit cum eo,
would sleep with him,
proximæ suæ exprobrat quod ea non sit digna habita,
she reproaches her neighbor because she was not found worthy,
sicut ipsa,
as she was,
neque funis ejus diruptus sit.
nor was her cord broken.
Omnia autem quæ illi fiunt,
But all things that occur with them are false;
falsa sunt:
in what way,
quomodo æstimandum
then,
aut dicendum est illos esse deos?
is it to be considered or said that they are gods?
A fabris autem et ab aurificibus facta sunt:
Yet they have been made by the workmen and the goldsmiths.
nihil aliud erunt, nisi id quod volunt esse sacerdotes.
They will be nothing else but what the priests want them to be.
Artifices etiam ipsi,
For the artisans themselves,
qui ea faciunt,
who make them,
non sunt multi temporis:
do not exist for a long time.
numquid ergo possunt ea,
So then, can these things,
quæ fabricata sunt ab ipsis,
which have been made by them,
esse dii?
be gods?
Reliquerunt autem falsa et opprobrium postea futuris.
Yet they have bequeathed falsehoods and disgrace after this to the future.
Nam cum supervenerit illis prælium et mala,
For when they are overcome by battle or evil,
cogitant sacerdotes apud se ubi se abscondant cum illis.
the priests consider among themselves where they may hide themselves with them.
Quomodo ergo sentiri debeant quoniam dii sunt,
Therefore, why would they be perceived to be gods,
qui nec de bello se liberant,
who can neither free themselves from war,
neque de malis se eripiunt?
nor rescue themselves from evils?
Nam cum sint lignea,
For, in as much as they are only wood,
inaurata et inargentata,
inlaid with gold and silver,
scietur postea quia falsa sunt ab universis gentibus et regibus:
so let it be known henceforth, by all nations and kings, that they are false;
quæ manifesta sunt quia non sunt dii,
because it has been revealed that they are not gods,
sed opera manuum hominum,
but the work of men’s hands,
et nullum Dei opus cum illis.
and there is no work of God in them.
Unde ergo notum est quia non sunt dii,
For this reason, then, it has been accepted that they are not gods,
sed opera manuum hominum,
but are works of the hands of men,
et nullum Dei opus in ipsis est.
and no work of God is in them.
Regem regioni non suscitant,
They have not raised up a king in the region,
neque pluviam hominibus dabunt.
nor will they give rain to men.
Judicium quoque non discernent,
They will not discern a judgment for anyone,
neque regiones liberabunt ab injuria,
nor will they free a region from injury,
quia nihil possunt,
because they can do nothing,
sicut corniculæ inter medium cæli et terræ.
like crows in the middle of heaven and earth.
Etenim cum inciderit ignis in domum deorum ligneorum,
And, indeed, when there happens to be a fire in the house of these gods of wood,
argenteorum et aureorum,
silver, and gold,
sacerdotes quidem ipsorum fugient, et liberabuntur:
the priests will certainly run away and save themselves,
ipsi vero sicut trabes in medio comburentur.
but these will truly be burned up like logs in the midst of it.
Regi autem
Yet they cannot withstand a king and war.
et bello non resistent.
In what way,
Quomodo ergo æstimandum est
then,
aut recipiendum quia dii sunt?
is it to be considered or accepted that they are gods?
Non a furibus, neque a latronibus se liberabunt dii lignei,
These gods of wood and stone, inlaid with gold and silver,
et lapidei, et inaurati, et inargentati:
can free themselves neither from thieves nor from robbers;
quibus hi qui fortiores sunt,
whoever is stronger than they are,
aurum et argentum,
will take up these things,
et vestimentum quo operti sunt,
the gold and the silver,
auferent illis,
and the garments which cover them,
et abibunt,
and will get away;
nec sibi auxilium ferent.
neither will they be able to help themselves.
Itaque melius est esse regem ostentantem virtutem suam,
Therefore, it is better to be a king displaying his power,
aut vas in domo utile,
or a useful vessel in a house,
in quo gloriabitur qui possidet illud,
about which he who owns it will boast,
vel ostium in domo,
or a door in the house,
quod custodit quæ in ipsa sunt, quam falsi dii.
which keeps safe what is inside, than to be these gods of falsehood.
Sol quidem et luna ac sidera,
For the sun, and the moon, and the constellations,
cum sint splendida et emissa ad utilitates,
though they are brilliant and have been sent forth to be useful,
obaudiunt:
are obedient.
similiter et fulgur cum apparuerit,
Similarly, the lightning, when it appears and is evident,
perspicuum est:
and, in like manner,
idipsum autem et spiritus in omni regione spirat:
the wind blowing in every region,
et nubes,
and the clouds,
quibus cum imperatum fuerit a Deo perambulare universum orbem,
when God orders them to make their rounds over the whole world,
perficiunt quod imperatum est eis:
each carries out what was commanded.
ignis etiam missus desuper,
Furthermore,
ut consumat montes
the fire,
et silvas,
having been sent from above so that it may consume mountains and woods,
facit quod præceptum est ei:
does what it has been instructed to do.
hæc autem
Yet these are not similar,
neque speciebus,
neither in splendor,
neque virtutibus,
nor in power,
uni eorum similia sunt.
to any one of them.
Unde
From this,
neque existimandum est,
it should neither be supposed,
neque dicendum illos esse deos,
nor said,
quando non possunt
that they are gods;
neque judicium judicare,
since they are neither able to give judgment,
neque quidquam facere hominibus.
nor to accomplish anything for men.
Scientes itaque quia non sunt dii,
And so, knowing that they are not gods,
ne ergo timueritis eos.
therefore, have no fear of them.
Neque enim regibus maledicent,
For they can neither curse kings,
neque benedicent.
nor bless them.
Signa etiam in cælo gentibus non ostendunt:
Besides, they show no signs in heaven to the nations;
neque ut sol lucebunt,
they neither shine like the sun,
neque illuminabunt ut luna.
nor give light like the moon.
Bestiæ meliores sunt illis,
Beasts are better than they are,
quæ possunt fugere sub tectum
for they can flee under a covering,
ac prodesse sibi.
and so protect themselves.
Nullo itaque modo nobis est manifestum quia sunt dii:
Therefore, in no way is it clear to us that they are gods;
propter quod ne timeatis eos.
because of this, you should not fear them.
Nam sicut in cucumerario formido nihil custodit,
For just as a scarecrow in a cucumber field protects nothing,
ita sunt dii illorum lignei,
so are their gods of wood,
et argentei,
and silver,
et inaurati.
and inlaid gold.
Eodem modo et in horto spina alba,
They are just the same as a white thorn in a garden,
supra quam omnis avis sedet,
on which all the birds sit;
similiter et mortuo projecto in tenebris,
they are even like a corpse thrown out into the darkness,
similes sunt dii illorum lignei,
just so are these gods of wood,
et inaurati,
and inlaid gold,
et inargentati.
and inlaid silver.
A purpura quoque
By the purple,
et murice,
and likewise the Royal purple,
quæ supra illos tineant,
moth-eaten garments upon them,
scietis itaque quia non sunt dii:
you will then know that they are not gods.
ipsi etiam postremo comeduntur,
And finally,
et erunt opprobrium in regione.
they themselves are consumed and will be a disgrace in the region.
Melior est homo justus qui non habet simulacra,
Better is the just man who has no such images,
nam erit longe ab opprobriis.
for he will be far from disgrace.”
